brief.headline: Indian Equities Eye Resistance Amid Global Tech Rout And Falling Crude
brief.summary: Nifty 50 and Bank Nifty closed higher as domestic banking and healthcare momentum remained resilient. However, global sentiment weakened sharply overnight with severe selloffs across Wall Street tech and Asian bourses following AI turmoil. Lower Brent crude and softening US 10-year yields offer domestic macro cushions ahead of key resistance tests.

takeaways.text: Nifty gained 2.61% last week to face resistance at 25,950–26,200, propelled by financials and healthcare.
Bank Nifty hit an intraday high of 64,485, gaining roughly 16% month-to-date across PSU and private lenders.
Wall Street suffered steep weekly losses with the Nasdaq 100 dropping 5.6% as tech and AI stocks slumped.
Anthropic's public debut collided with an estimated $4 trillion AI wipeout and continued pressure on Nvidia.
Brent crude dipped to $89.95, though analysts warn levels near $91 still pose inflation risks for India.
Ashoka Buildcon lost a ₹846.38 crore Saudi Arabia construction contract following project cancellation by Diriyah Company.

sections.india: Domestic equities maintained upward momentum with Nifty advancing 2.61% last week to close at 25800.6, testing resistance bands between 25,950 and 26,200. Nifty Bank rose around 16% month-to-date, propelled by heavy buying across both PSU and private banking majors. Hospital and healthcare stocks surged up to 14% over five trading sessions on solid earnings visibility. On the macro front, Brent crude hovered near $89.95, while paint companies eye volume recovery amid sticky input costs.
sections.world: Global markets endured significant pressure as the S&P 500 and Dow Jones fell into correction territory, declining 3.70% and 1.93% respectively. Tech equities faced intense liquidation, with the Nasdaq sliding 5.28% in its worst weekly performance since March 2020. Asian indices tracked the weakness as the Nikkei 225 tumbled 5.06% and the Hang Seng retreated 1.89%. Treasury yields fell as the US 10-year yield shed 14.0 bps to 4.91% amid shifting rate expectations.
sections.tech: Anthropic completed its historic Nasdaq debut, but its listing failed to halt an estimated $4 trillion AI market wipeout. Hardware giant Nvidia faces multiple headwinds, including extended weekly stock declines, leadership changes, and a California state probe evaluating potential criminal violations. Meanwhile, Amazon is nearing a $7.5bn acquisition of AI start-up Decart to boost cloud computing power. Cyber consolidation picked up as CrowdStrike engaged in discussions with Zscaler to address sophisticated AI-driven threats.

stories.title: Crude prices may normalise to USD 70 by end-2027 as global oil market moves into surplus: Report
stories.summary: Global crude oil prices are projected to normalize around USD 70 per barrel by the end of 2027. Rising non-OPEC+ supplies and declining Chinese oil demand are expected to lead to a market surplus. Refining margins are likely to remain elevated in the near term before gradual normalization occurs. Geopolitical tensions, particularly between the US and Iran, are likely to influence oil supply dynamics.
stories.ai_summary: A report projects global crude prices will normalize to around USD 70 per barrel by end-2027 due to market surpluses. Non-OPEC+ supply growth and cooling Chinese demand are expected to drive the shift.
stories.why_it_matters: Positive for Indian OMCs, paints, and specialty chemicals on projected medium-term input relief.
